faq: Which CRM do you train on?
Whichever one you use, as long as we can view it with you on a screen share. We prepare using your own settings and sample deals, so the training matches what your team sees every day.
Do you train in a different time zone?
We find a time that suits your team inside the delivery window and confirm it in writing. Sessions are live over video, and recordings are shared afterwards for anyone who could not attend.
Do you change my CRM settings?
Training does not change your setup. If we spot a setting that confuses people, we note it for you and you can order a fix as a separate service, such as CRM Setup or Pipeline Stages.
How do I get my team to use it daily?
We keep the daily actions to a short list, show the benefit to each role and agree one simple rule, such as no deal without a next step. Managers get tips for checking the data weekly.

desc:
CRM team training sessions teach your people to use the CRM every day, using your own deals and stages. Ecom Swift LLC runs short live sessions by video, shares recordings and leaves a one page cheat sheet for everyone.

## Why do teams stop using their CRM?

Teams stop using a CRM because it feels like extra work with no reward. Nobody showed them the five quick actions that matter, so they guess, make mistakes and revert to spreadsheets and memory. Then managers see empty fields and conclude the tool failed.

Usually the tool is fine. What was missing was a short, practical introduction that connects the CRM to the person's own day.

## What untrained users cost you

When half the team uses the CRM and half does not, the data becomes unreliable. Deals are missing, notes are in the wrong place and reports describe only part of the business. Managers either stop trusting the numbers or spend their time chasing updates by message.

There is a hidden cost as well. The money spent on the subscription and setup returns nothing if people avoid the tool. A small amount of training protects a larger investment.

## How practical training changes behavior

People adopt tools that make their own work easier. Training on real deals shows each person how the CRM helps them: where to see today's tasks, how to log a call in a few seconds, how to move a deal and how to find a customer's history before a call.

Short sessions work better than long lectures because attention fades. Practice tasks turn instructions into habit, and recordings let new hires catch up without a new session. A data entry rules document settles the small arguments about how to write names, notes and stage updates, which keeps the records tidy as the team grows.

## What good CRM training includes

- A live session by video, held on your real CRM, not a demo account.
- A focus on the five or six actions your team needs every day.
- Content split by role, so sales staff and managers learn what is relevant to them.
- Practice tasks with feedback, using your own sample deals.
- Time for questions as they arise.
- A recording of each session, shared with the team.
- A one page cheat sheet for the desk or the screen.
- Role guides and a document of data entry rules.
- A way to handle new hires afterward without repeating everything.

## How we run it

We start by asking what your team does in the CRM and where people struggle. Then we prepare the session around your actual stages, fields and deals, so nothing feels abstract. Sessions are live, friendly and practical. We show an action, then people do it themselves, and we answer questions on the spot.

The Basic package is a single session and a cheat sheet for a small group. Standard adds sessions split by role, practice tasks with feedback and shared recordings. Premium offers a full training week, role guides, a data entry rules document and set times for follow-up questions. If you work across time zones, we can agree a slot that suits your team, which we confirm before booking. Training does not change your CRM settings, since configuration is a separate service.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Ask the whole team to attend, including managers.
- Use real deals during the session.
- Tell people in advance what the CRM replaces, such as a spreadsheet.
- Have managers use the CRM visibly in meetings.
- Share the recording and cheat sheet straight after.

**Avoid:**
- Teaching every feature in one sitting.
- Training before the CRM is set up properly.
- Making the CRM an extra step on top of the old habits instead of replacing them.
- Skipping new hires who join after the session.
- Punishing mistakes instead of fixing the cause.

## Who this service is for

It suits a team that has just had a CRM set up and needs everyone to start on the same footing. It suits a business where the CRM exists but half the staff ignore it. It also suits a manager who is about to hire several people and wants a repeatable way to onboard them.

## What we need from you

Tell us which CRM you use, who will attend and what each role does. Send a few sample deals or a short list of daily tasks, and tell us your time zone and the times that suit your team. We teach on your own account, so a view-only or user login for us is enough, and we never need your password. If you want settings changed afterward, we handle that as a separate piece of work.
